name: perturbation-demo
title: Perturbation demo — gene knockouts and media shifts on the baseline whole cell

glossary.definition: Setting a gene's translation efficiency to zero on the cached initiation config, so the transcript is made but no protein -- a loss-of-function without a ParCa re-fit.
The lactose-permease gene, used as the demo knockout target; a membrane transporter whose loss is near-neutral on glucose medium.
Changing the simulated growth medium (e.g. adding amino acids to minimal M9) to perturb the environment rather than the genome.
Guanosine tetraphosphate, the stringent-response alarmone; high under nutrient limitation, it throttles ribosome synthesis. Amino-acid supplementation lowers it and speeds growth.
The pre-computed parameter-calculation output reused by both levers, so a perturbation is a one-line config variant with no re-fit.

biological_story:
The v2ecoli baseline is a wild-type E. coli cell; a perturbation asks how that cell responds when one thing changes. This demo uses two minimal, biologically distinct levers.

A translation-level gene knockout zeroes the translation efficiency of a named gene on the cached polypeptide-initiation config, so its mRNA is still transcribed but no protein is synthesized -- the phenotype of a loss-of-function mutant without re-fitting the model. lacY, the lactose permease, is a convenient demo target: knocking it out removes a membrane transporter with little cost on glucose medium.

A media shift instead changes the environment the same genome sees: supplementing the minimal medium with amino acids relieves the cell of synthesizing them de novo, which lowers ppGpp, up-regulates ribosome synthesis, and speeds growth. Both levers reuse the existing ParCa cache -- no parameter re-fit -- so each perturbation is a one-line variant on the baseline, making them ideal for showing how genotype and environment separately move a whole-cell phenotype.
question: How do you apply a gene knockout or a media change to the v2ecoli baseline, minimally?

executive.what_is_this:
A minimal, self-contained demonstration of the two lightweight perturbation
levers built directly into the `baseline` composite. Both reuse the existing
ParCa cache — no re-fit — so each perturbation is a one-line variant:

  - `knockouts`: translation-level gene knockouts. Each named gene's
    translation efficiency is zeroed on the cached polypeptide-initiation
    config, so no protein is made — a functional knockout with no ParCa
    re-fit. (Folded in from the former KO_baseline composite.)
  - `media`: an in-cache media shift. The environment's initial media_id is
    set to any condition in the cache's saved_media, so the media_update step
    moves the cell onto that condition on the first tick and metabolism
    responds (e.g. amino-acid-rich media grows faster).

The single study `ko-and-media` runs the wild-type baseline against a lacY
knockout and an amino-acid-rich medium, side by side. This is a starting
point / how-to for perturbing the whole cell — not a rigorous result. For a
rigorously-calibrated media condition, run a per-condition ParCa cache
instead (see the whole-cell-model-comparison investigation's succinate study).

studies.name: ko-and-media
studies.title: Knockout and media perturbations on the baseline whole cell
studies.question:
How do a translation-level gene knockout (lacY) and an amino-acid-rich medium
each move the v2ecoli baseline off its wild-type trajectory — and how do you
express each as a one-line variant of the baseline composite?

findings.statement: baseline(knockouts=['EG10526']) zeroes exactly the lacY translation efficiency on the live process; growth is unchanged in glucose-minimal (correct — lacY is dispensable without lactose).

baseline(media='minimal_plus_amino_acids') reaches +46.99% dry mass vs +43.89% for minimal over 1500 steps (diverges from ~step 450) — the in-cache media shift takes effect via media_update without a ParCa re-fit.
